attempts.label: CRCNS:fcx-1
attempts.paper_title: Network Homeostasis and State Dynamics of Neocortical Sleep
attempts.entry_title: Network homeostasis and state dynamics of neocortical sleep (Watson et al. 2016)
attempts.summary: The paper's central finding, that sleep evens out cortical firing as fast-firing pyramidal cells slow down and slow-firing cells speed up, held up in this data across sleep and within nonREM packets (first-to-last packet slope 0.872), as did the overall decline in population rate. The reported drop in rate variability over sleep and the firing changes within single UP states did not reproduce. Most of the lasting effects of individual sub-states (REM, microarousals, waking between packets) did not reproduce, likely because the paper does not say how sequences of states were formed and no rule gave its cell counts. Lower firing in waking after sleep held only weakly, as most cycles lack scored waking right after sleep.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Watson, Levenstein, Greene, Gelinas and Buzsaki (2016) on CRCNS data set fcx-1, which holds the spike trains, scored brain states, detected UP/DOWN states and spindles, and LFP of 27 frontal cortex recordings in 11 rats. It compares firing rates across states, their changes over sleep and within nonREM episodes and packets, the LFP and UP/DOWN dynamics, and the rate changes across sleep sub-state triplets.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Watson et al. (2016) from CRCNS fcx-1

outcomes.notes: 995 pE and 126 pI cells (mean 36.85 pE per session, range 10 to 104; pI mean 4.67, range 0 to 13), 27 sessions and 11 rats match exactly. The WAKE-SLEEP cycles in _WSRestrictedIntervals.mat number 51, not 54; each session's Wake and Sleep intervals are exactly its WakeSleep pairs (51, 51 and 51 in all), with no unpaired WAKE or SLEEP, so no cycle was lost in parsing. The criterion names no partial outcome; partial is given because five of six counts match, and whether a partial rule applies is asked of a reader.

434 MA intervals lie inside SLEEP (2130 in the files). Median duration 11.0 s over all MAs (11.5 s over session medians), per-session median incidence 0.184 per minute, per-session median 3.70% of SLEEP, against 790, 15.9 s, 0.32 and 9.1%; none within tolerance. The MA fraction falls over normalized episodes (20 bins, bin means R = -0.956, p = 4.5e-11; 10 bins R = -0.970, p = 3.3e-06), and over SLEEP the bin means are not significant (p = 0.15, 0.098; pooled period-bins p = 0.0057, 0.00061). The criterion names no partial outcome; partial is given because the trends hold and the four values do not. The 345 WakeInterruptions shorter than 40 s are not MAs by the paper's definition, since none lies between two packets (123 between two REM intervals, 80 between REM and a packet). Variant, MA reading (b), counting them as MAs, 779 events, 0.318 per minute (within tolerance), median 13.0 s, 7.85% of SLEEP, episodes R = -0.960 (p = 1.9e-11), SLEEP p = 0.93. With the Dino ACC sessions left out, episodes R = -0.949 (p = 1.7e-10), SLEEP p = 0.089.
deviations: The episode correlation uses the MA fraction in 10 or 20 normalized bins, both as bin means over episodes and as pooled episode-bins, as the criterion allows; episodes include MA and packet seconds.

outcomes.notes: Median of the 701 packets in SLEEP 111.0 s. Longest over shortest 52.5 (14 to 735 s), less than the two orders of magnitude of the statement, which the criterion only reports.

Reading (a) medians pE 0.755, 0.706, 0.936 Hz and pI 6.001, 4.565, 5.724 Hz; reading (b) pE 0.784, 0.691, 0.922 and pI 5.632, 4.637, 5.724. Five of six within 10% under both; pI REM is 5.724 against 4.25. pE skew 2.18 to 2.83. The 1st to 99th percentile range covers 0.05 to 5 Hz within 10% in WAKE (0.004 to 7.14 Hz, reading b) and REM (0.008 to 6.03) but not nonREM (0.014 to 4.17; 4.05 under reading a); 5th to 95th percentiles stop below 4.5 Hz in every state. The criterion requires the shape for both the reproduced and the partial outcome, so the outcome is not reproduced. Whether the range applies to each state, when the paper itself says the nonREM tail is shorter, is asked of a reader. The pI REM median is equal under both readings because the middle cell is the same (Dino_061814_mPFC cell 46, 5.706 and 5.743 Hz in its two cycles); reading (a) has no duplicated rows.
deviations: The range test is applied in each state, as the criterion's 'in each state' reads.

outcomes.notes: Reading (a) slope of log10 nonREM on log10 WAKE 0.684 (0.661 to 0.708), R 0.803; reading (b) 0.687 (0.658 to 0.717), R 0.824. Linear rates give slope 0.45. 82% of cells above the median WAKE rate fire less in nonREM, 55% of those below fire more.
Reading (a) 18.8% WAKE, 20.6% REM, 9.3% nonREM; chi-square nonREM against WAKE p = 4.1e-16, against REM p = 4.4e-21. Reading (b) fractions 18.4, 19.5, 9.1% with p = 3.2e-09 and 8.3e-11.

Medians (nonREM, WAKE, REM) reading (a) 6.26, 2.43, 3.56%; (b) 4.93, 1.58, 2.33%; (c) 11.47, 4.51, 6.39%. Kruskal-Wallis p from 3.4e-46 to 3.6e-54; REM above WAKE by Dunn (p 1.3e-06 to 1e-05) and rank-sum. The order and the tests hold under every reading; no reading puts all three medians within tolerance.
deviations: Reading (c), the fraction of spikes with an ISI <= 15 ms before or after them, is added from the Results' wording, 'the fraction of spikes with ISIs below 15 ms' (Results, Assessment of firing patterns in different brain states), beside the claims file's readings of a proportion of ISIs.

outcomes.notes: Average nonREM autocorrelogram peaks at 8.5 ms; WAKE and REM have local maxima at 125 and 126 ms (nonREM also at 125 ms). Median decay, reading (a) WAKE -0.108, nonREM -0.538, REM -0.169; (b) -0.118, -0.336, -0.112; (c) -0.582, -1.623, -0.574. nonREM is the most negative and Kruskal-Wallis p <= 1.7e-95 under all three; no medians within tolerance. Cells with fewer than 100 counts dropped (158 of 995 in WAKE, 131 in nonREM, 284 in REM). The 125 ms bump is small, the average autocorrelogram at 115 to 135 ms being 1.027 (WAKE), 1.026 (REM) and 0.981 (nonREM) times its mean at 80 to 100 and 150 to 170 ms; the local-maximum test also fires at 125 ms in nonREM.
deviations: Per-cell peaks are found on a 5 ms boxcar-smoothed autocorrelogram in 1 to 50 ms, and cells with fewer than 100 counts are dropped; both are standard choices the paper does not state.

outcomes.notes: Reading (a) 62.9% of pE cells fire with another pE cell in at most 4% of windows and 0.00% in at least half; reading (b) 54.2% and 0.00%. Per-cell distributions skewed (2.31, 2.26); population synchrony per window skew 1.28. The criterion's bounds hold with wide margins.
Deposited detections, 43230 UP and 86839 DOWN states (the paper's counts exactly), medians 0.473 and 0.188 s, skew 2.56 and 2.15. All start inside scored packets of the cycles.
deviations: Uses the deposited UP/DOWN detections (_UPDOWNINtervals.mat), reading (a) of updown-durations; a new detection was not run, since the LFP reduction kept has no power above 100 Hz.

outcomes.notes: Per normalized bin over 43230 UP states, pE rate 1.823, 1.359 ... 1.310, 1.619 Hz (last not below the first two; R = -0.293); pI 15.88 to 11.63 Hz (R = -0.983); synchrony 0.079 to 0.071 (last below first two, R = -0.447); E/(E+I) 0.373 to 0.396 (R = +0.470). Sigma power peaks in bin 0 and gamma in bin 3, the reverse of the statement. Two of four measures decrease and the spectral order fails.
deviations: The criterion's 50 ms bins for synchrony and E/(E+I) are taken as the 10 normalized UP-state bins (47 ms for a median UP state).

Gamma and sigma power come from an 8 ms band-power series (4th order Butterworth, mean of the squared signal) on goodeegchannel, log10 and z-scored per session; the paper's spectrogram method is not given.
Uses the deposited UP/DOWN detections (_UPDOWNINtervals.mat), reading (a) of updown-durations; a new detection was not run, since the LFP reduction kept has no power above 100 Hz.

The 8 ms series is zero-phase band-passed, which at 9 to 25 Hz spreads power over tens of ms, so the sigma peak in the first bin may carry power from the DOWN-UP edge; the outcome fails on the pE rate and E/(E+I) regardless.

outcomes.notes: First and second half latencies correlate across cells, R = 0.733 (halves of each SLEEP, n 932) and 0.660 (halves of the session, n 758). Latency against log10 WAKE rate R = -0.127, p = 7.6e-05; against log10 nonREM rate R = -0.238, p = 6e-14. Per session the WAKE-rate correlation is negative in 20 of 27 sessions.
deviations: A cell's mean latency in a half is computed when it has at least 5 UP states with a spike within 200 ms (a standard choice).

outcomes.notes: Mean 100 ms count correlations in nonREM, WAKE sextiles, 6-6 0.0328 (p = 2.9e-70), 1-1 0.0062 (p = 2.1e-20), 1-6 0.0064 (p = 2e-12, positive). Correlations rise with rate group across the whole matrix; no negative group pair. nonREM sextiles, the claims file's reading (b) for this figure, give 1-6 0.0095 (p = 8.5e-66).
deviations: Sextiles follow M2. Reading (a) ranks each pE cell's rate over all scored WAKE of its session (before round 1's revision, the mean of its per-cycle WAKE rates, which put 65 of 995 cells in another sextile); reading (b) ranks each cell's rate in each cycle's WAKE and uses the cycle that holds the analysed period.

outcomes.notes: Normalized mean pE rate against normalized SLEEP time, clock (i), R = -0.273 (a, p = 1.7e-13), -0.154 (b, p = 2.5e-57), -0.732 (c, p = 1.5e-09); clock (ii) R = -0.283, -0.163, -0.796. By rat (reading b) the decline is significant in 8 of 11 rats; Rizzo, Splinter and Templeton show R = -0.017, -0.049, -0.014.
deviations: Trends over normalized time follow M3 and M4 of the claims file; every reading (a, b, c) is run and, for SLEEP and episodes, two normalization clocks, (i) the period's clock time and (ii) the cumulative time of the used state, since the paper says only that SLEEP is time-normalized with nonREM time used (Results, Firing pattern and LFP changes across the course of sleep; Fig. 3B legend). Values are divided by the session mean before pooling (M3).

outcomes.notes: Reading (a) first 1.027 +- 1.086, last 0.905 +- 0.936 Hz, signed-rank p = 1e-18; reading (b) 1.048 and 0.883 Hz, signed-rank p = 1.9e-20, rank-sum p = 0.0012. All 51 SLEEP periods have at least 2 packets.

Only 23 cycles have a scored WAKE after their SLEEP; in 17 it starts 166 to 10344 s later. pE rates are lower after, signed-rank p = 0.018 (reading a, 703 cell-cycles) and 0.048 (b, 494 cells); rank-sum p = 0.95 and 0.98. Whether that is the paper's window is asked of a reader; the outcome is the claims file's reading.

outcomes.notes: Deposited spindles (5201 of 5203 start in nonREM of SLEEP); per-session mean incidence 2.852 +- 0.490 per minute, duration 0.616 s, frequency 13.923 Hz, amplitude 208.4 uV. Frequency and amplitude match; incidence matches Table S1 (0.049 Hz, 2.94 per minute) not the Results' 1.94; duration is outside 0.52 +- 0.052. Incidence over SLEEP, reading (b) R = -0.021, p = 0.03 (partial by M4); (a) p = 0.44; (c) p = 0.66; clock (ii) p >= 0.19. Absence of change holds for duration (p >= 0.068, clock i) but frequency changes under (b) (p = 0.011) and amplitude under (a) (p = 0.047). Over all 5201 spindles the duration is 0.614 +- 0.320 s, median 0.524 s, which matches the paper's 0.52 +- 0.32. With the two Dino ACC sessions left out, the incidence decrease is not significant (reading b p = 0.15).
deviations: Uses the deposited spindle detections (_Spindles.mat), reading (a) of the criterion; a new detection was not run. Amplitude converted from V to uV.

Trends over normalized time follow M3 and M4 of the claims file; every reading (a, b, c) is run and, for SLEEP and episodes, two normalization clocks, (i) the period's clock time and (ii) the cumulative time of the used state, since the paper says only that SLEEP is time-normalized with nonREM time used (Results, Firing pattern and LFP changes across the course of sleep; Fig. 3B legend). The outcome depends on the normalization clock, which the paper does not state (Results; Fig. 3B legend); clock (i), the period's clock time, and clock (ii), the cumulative nonREM time, give different outcomes here. As for every trend, the outcome takes the result under one of them, as M4 does for readings; the question is put to the paper's authors.

The incidence decrease also depends on the two Dino days that were recorded with two probes and are deposited as two sessions each (ACC and mPFC); without the ACC copies, reading (b) clock (i) gives p = 0.15. Both copies are kept, since the paper's 27 sessions, which the data set matches, include them.

findings.statement: The files hold 51 WAKE-SLEEP cycles (WakeSleepTimePairFormat over the 27 sessions), where the paper reports 54; the Wake and Sleep intervals are the same 51 pairs, with none unpaired. All other counts (995 pE, 126 pI, 27 sessions, 11 rats, 43230 UP and 86839 DOWN states, 5203 spindles) match the paper exactly.

The paper reports 790 microarousals; 434 MA intervals lie inside SLEEP (2130 MA intervals in the files, most outside SLEEP). 345 WakeInterruption intervals inside SLEEP are shorter than the 40 s minimum the data description gives for them; none lies between two packets (123 between two REM intervals, 80 between REM and a packet), so they are not MAs by the paper's definition either, though counted with the MAs they give 779 events. One nonREM packet (14 s) is shorter than the 20 s minimum of Table S1.

In Rizzo_022715 and Splinter_020515 a WAKE-SLEEP cycle's WAKE starts before the previous cycle's SLEEP ends (WAKE 9919-14394 s against SLEEP 5655-10010 s; WAKE 5335-7210 s against SLEEP 3543-5455 s), so the cycles overlap.

Dino_061914 and Dino_062014 each appear as two sessions, ACC and mPFC probes recorded at the same time (the data set's WatsonSleepHomestasis2016Table.xlsx lists the same days), each with its own state files, and the two scorings of Dino_062014 differ (mean SLEEP per cycle 59.5 min in ACC and 27.1 min in mPFC; 41 and 17 packets). State- and LFP-level analyses over the 27 sessions count these days twice.
The data description says the motion signal in _Motion.mat is z-scored; it is non-negative in every session, with per-session means from 0.55 to 4076, and BWRat19_032513 holds NaN values.

RecordingFileIntervals in _BasicMetaData.mat ends at infinity in the three sessions of rat JennBuzsaki22, and the UP/DOWN file is named _UPDOWNINtervals.mat, where the description says _UPDOWNInts.mat and _UPDOWNIntervals.mat.
The Results give spindle incidence as 1.94 +- 0.39 per minute; Table S1 gives 0.049 +- 0.008 Hz (2.94 per minute). The deposited spindles give 2.85 per minute, matching Table S1.

Scored WAKE exists only as the WAKE of a WAKE-SLEEP cycle, so the WAKE that follows a SLEEP is in most cycles absent or hours later (23 of 51 cycles have a later scored WAKE, 6 within 1 s). The 5 min post-sleep WAKE windows of the paper cannot be located for most cycles.

Each session is one tar.gz of 0.9 to 6 GB, and the order of members differs between files (the LFP .eeg comes before the spike and state files in some), so reading any one small file needs the whole archive streamed. Reading all 27 takes 7 to 9 minutes from the bucket.

Questions for the paper's authors. (1) The sampling unit of the correlations against normalized time (per packet, 10 s bins, or bins of normalized time averaged over periods) and whether SLEEP is normalized by its clock time or by its concatenated nonREM time; the readings give different outcomes for the CV, spindle and UP/DOWN trends over SLEEP. (2) Whether the burst index is the proportion of ISIs <= 15 ms (Supplemental Experimental Procedures) or the fraction of spikes with such an ISI (Results); the latter gives the reported nonREM median. (3) The model and fit range of the autocorrelogram decay exponent. (4) How triplets are formed (adjacency of scored intervals, which WAKE counts between packets, giving the 24 nonREM-WAKE-nonREM triplets) and whether REM-packet-REM triplets allow an arousal after the first REM; the attempt assumes they do, which gives 80 triplets and 660 cells against the about 136 cells of Figure S5D. (5) Whether the motion signal was z-scored before the movement correlation. (6) How the WAKE sextiles are computed for cells recorded over several cycles (session WAKE or each cycle's WAKE); fig3e-wake-before-after-sextiles and fig3f-within-up-changes differ between the two.

verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The first executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. Its report had no attempt record and gave its own outcome for each claim; 35 of 41 agree with the record as it then stood.

disagreements.reason: Cell 11, from the files' MA intervals, n 434 (790), median 11.0 s (15.9), 0.184/min (0.32) and 3.7% (9.1) are all outside tolerance. The episode trend holds (20 bins R -0.956, p 4.5e-11), and the SLEEP trend shows no change on bin means (p 0.10-0.15).

Cell 16, 5 of 6 medians are within tolerance (pI REM 5.72 vs 4.25 is not). The shape test fails because the nonREM pE range stops short of 4.5 Hz under both percentile readings (1-99th; 4.05 and 4.17 Hz). See B11 on the criterion.

Cell 65 (b), all four increases are below their bounds and all four durations are within tolerance. The packet frequency does change (p 0.0096), against the absence claim, but the criterion's final rule leaves this part out.
Cell 69 (b), all sextile, CV and burst parts hold under clock (ii). Under clock (i) the episode burst p is 2.6e-10, just above the 1e-10 bound.
Cell 71, 3 of 6 meet their bounds; the criterion needs 4. All six have the right sign at p < 0.05.

Cell 85, 8 or 52 triplets (paper 24). The fastest sextile does not increase. Motion vs change; R 0.48, p 0.28 with raw motion. Raw motion is pooled across sessions whose means run from 0.55 to 4076; pooled that way the correlation is not meaningful. The z-scored variant matches the data description's own definition and would make the claim partially reproduced, but it rests on only n = 7 (B4).

entries.name: crcns-fcx-1-watson-2016
entries.title: Network homeostasis and state dynamics of neocortical sleep (Watson et al. 2016)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Watson, Levenstein, Greene, Gelinas and Buzsaki (2016) on CRCNS data set fcx-1, which holds the spike trains, scored brain states, detected UP/DOWN states and spindles, and LFP of 27 frontal cortex recordings in 11 rats. It compares firing rates across states, their changes over sleep and within nonREM episodes and packets, the LFP and UP/DOWN dynamics, and the rate changes across sleep sub-state triplets.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Watson et al. (2016) from CRCNS fcx-1
